{{Quote|So what exactly did the kid say that set you off, Col? In all the excitement I missed that.|John D. Branon, asking Col Takbright what Luke Skywalker had told him during the briefing|<ref name="DutyRoster" />}}
'''John D. Branon''' was a young [[human]] [[rebel pilot]] who was a member of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] against the [[Galactic Empire]]. While stationed on the [[moon]] [[Yavin 4]], Branon and other [[pilot]]s would lecture fellow pilot [[Col Takbright]] following the latter's emotional outbursts. He was later curious to learn what had occurred between Takbright and pilot [[Luke Skywalker]] in [[General]] [[Jan Dodonna]]'s briefing prior to the [[Battle of Yavin]]. Through his insistence, Branon successfully coaxed him into revealing the fact.

He was later selected to participate in the battle as part of [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]], members of which considered him a veteran, under the [[callsign]] [[Red Four]] by the [[squadron]]'s [[Red Leader|leader]], [[Garven Dreis]]. During the battle, Red Squadron broke away from formation to draw enemy fire away from the accompanying [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]]. Branon then came under fire from one of the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] that had arrived and was [[Death|killed]] when it shot down his [[T-65B X-wing starfighter|X-wing]].

==Biography==
===Stationed on Yavin 4===
{{Quote|Takbright! You still haven't told us what the kid said.|John D. Branon, to Takbright|<ref name="DutyRoster" />}}
[[File:Red_Squadron_SWCT.png|thumb|left|250px|Branon was considered a veteran by members of Red Squadron.]]
John D. Branon was a young<ref name="SWCT" /> [[Rebel pilot|pilot]] who was a member of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] fought against the [[Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Episode IV" /> By [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Film Date">{{Film|IV|1}}</ref> he<ref name="SWCT" /> was considered a veteran by the [[pilot]]s of [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]] and was stationed at their [[Great Temple|base]] on the [[moon]] [[Yavin 4]]. He—along with fellow pilots [[Puck Naeco]], [[General]] [[Antoc Merrick]], and Red Squadron's [[Red Leader|leader]], [[Garven Dreis]]—would lecture fellow Red Squadron member [[Col Takbright]] after the latter's hotheaded outbursts.<ref name="DutyRoster" />

Shortly after the [[Battle of Scarif]]<ref name="DutyRoster" /> of 1 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]],<ref name="Scarif Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> in which the [[Death Star plans|technical readouts]] of the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[battle station]] were stolen by the Rebel Alliance,<ref name="Rogue One">''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref> General [[Jan Dodonna]] assembled the Yavin pilots and briefed them on how they would destroy the [[superweapon]]: the pilots would exploit a two-[[meter]]–wide [[thermal exhaust port]] to cause a cataclysmic [[Reactor|main reactor]] failure. The [[Death Star]] was rapidly approaching Yavin 4 and threatened to destroy the base, thus necessitating its [[Battle of Yavin|destruction]].<ref name="Episode IV" /> The pilots, including Branon, Naeco, Takbright, and [[Theron Nett]], gathered in the [[squadron]]'s ready room, waiting to receive their assignments and man their [[starfighter]]s. When Naeco teased Takbright regarding his nickname, "Fake Wedge," Branon and Nett exchanged an amused glance. Afterward, the pilots discussed the chances of successfully destroying the Death Star with a precise hit from a [[proton torpedo]].<ref name="DutyRoster" />

[[File:DeathStar_plans.png|thumb|right|300px|Branon was curious to learn what Luke Skywalker had said during the briefing.]]
Branon asked Takbright what the squadron's newest pilot, [[Luke Skywalker]], had told him during the briefing, to which Takbright replied that he himself had loudly stated that it was impossible to score a hit on a two-meter target, even for a [[computer]]. He then asked Branon if he had the same doubts about the mission, to which Branon was ambivalent. As more pilots entered the room, Takbright told Branon to forget whatever had happened during the briefing. However, Branon was still insistent on learning what Skywalker had said, and Takbright finally relented; he revealed that Skywalker used to [[Hunting|hunt]] [[womp rat]]s in his [[Luke's T-16 skyhopper|T-16 skyhopper]]. After Dreis arrived, Branon was selected to fly in the attack on the [[Space station|battle station]] under the [[callsign]] [[Red Four]] alongside pilot [[Harb Binli]], flying as [[Red Seven]]. They were both chosen to serve as [[Wingmate|wingmen]] to [[Major]] [[Ralo Surrel]], who was given the callsign [[Red Eleven]], for the [[second flight]].<ref name="DutyRoster" />

===Battle of Yavin and death===
{{Quote|I'm hit!|Branon's last words|audio=ImHit-ANH.flac|<ref name="Episode IV" />}}
After preparations were complete, the pilots of both Red Squadron and [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]] entered their respective [[T-65B X-wing starfighter|X-wings]] and [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber|Y-wings]] and took off from the Yavin 4 base to begin the Battle of Yavin. As the pilots approached the Death Star in the [[Yavin system]], Red Squadron broke away from formation to draw the Death Star's [[turbolaser]] fire away from Gold Squadron while the latter began its attack run in the superweapon's [[meridian trench]]. During the battle, the Empire scrambled several [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] to engage them.<ref name="Episode IV" />

[[File:Branon-Death.png|thumb|left|300px|Branon perishes over the Death Star.]]
As the [[TIE series|TIEs]] neared the rebel [[Starship|craft]],<ref name="Episode IV" /> Branon and Nett were targeted early in the attack.<ref name="SWCT" /> Branon then came under fire from one of the Imperial vessels. Attempting to evade the enemy fighter on his tail, he<ref name="Episode IV" /> desperately<ref name="Topps B&W">{{Topps|set=2018 Topps Star Wars Black & White: A New Hope|cardname=Red Four: John D. Branon|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/159376/cid/10752397}}</ref> exclaimed he was hit as his [[X-wing starfighter|X-wing]] was shot down, bursting into [[Fire|flames]] and [[Death|killing]] him.<ref name="Episode IV" /> He thus became the first Red Squadron pilot to be hit by TIE fire in the battle, and most of the squadron also lost their lives in the engagement, including Dreis, Nett, Naeco, and Branon's wingmen Surrel and Binli.<ref name="DutyRoster" /> During the battle, Branon's death was reported by a [[Unidentified control officer|control officer]] back at the Yavin 4 base. The [[officer]]'s communication log was included in a partial transcript of recordings from the base's war room that was later added to a collection of non-electronic documents known as ''[[The Rebel Files]]''.<ref name="Rebel Files">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref> Ultimately, the rebels emerged victorious when Skywalker, who flew as [[Red Five]], managed to score a precise hit on the Death Star's [[Temperature|thermal]] exhaust port and obliterate the superweapon completely.<ref name="Episode IV" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|To Dreis, Branon, Porkins, Rue, Dinnes, Naytaan, Nett, Surrel, Naeco…|Skywalker, honoring Branon and Red Squadron's actions|<ref name="Star Wars 45">[[Star Wars (2015) 45|''Star Wars'' (2015) 45]]</ref>}}
Branon's participation in the battle marked him as a rebel hero, with his callsign going along with the legend.<ref name="SWCT" /> By at least [[0 ABY]],<ref name="Luke & Leia Date">''[[Choose Your Destiny: A Luke & Leia Adventure]]'' takes place between the events of {{Film|IV}} and {{Film|V}}, which corresponds to the [[time]] period between [[0 ABY]] and [[3 ABY]] per ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''.</ref> the [[Twi'lek]] [[Bela Elar]] served as Red Four in Red Squadron.<ref name="A Luke & Leia Adventure">''[[Choose Your Destiny: A Luke & Leia Adventure]]''</ref> In [[1 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars (2015) 45|''Star Wars'' (2015) 45]] to [[1 ABY]].</ref> Skywalker and fellow rebels [[Han Solo]], [[Wedge Antilles]], [[Zev Senesca]], [[Derek Klivian]], and [[Chewbacca]] raised a [[Toast (ritual)|toast]] at [[Mess Hall IV]] in the [[Mako-Ta Space Docks]] to honor the deceased members of Red Squadron, including Branon.<ref name="Star Wars 45" />

==Personality and traits==
Branon was a [[human]] with [[Color|light]] skin.<ref name="Episode IV" /> Shrewd and rigorous,<ref name="Odyssey">''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]''</ref> he was cautious and was not overly optimistic toward the rebels' chances against the Death Star. Branon also showed an inquisitive side, curious to know what had happened in the briefing room between Takbright and Skywalker much to the irritation of the former, who likened him to a "[[nek]] with a [[bone]]." He would also lecture Takbright after his outbursts and had a silent way of sternly calming the pilot down.<ref name="DutyRoster" /> Like other Rebel Alliance personnel, he realized that [[the galaxy]] would be left in fear if the Death Star continued fully functioning and hoped that General Dodonna's plan to destroy the superweapon would succeed.<ref name="2018 Files">{{Topps|set=2018 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files|cardname=John D. Branon—Red Ten|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/170092/cid/11689230}}</ref>

==Skills and abilities==
Branon was considered by members of Red Squadron to be a veteran.<ref name="DutyRoster" /> He had above-average intelligence, [[Diplomat|diplomacy]] skills, strength, speed, and fighting ability. He was not [[Force-sensitive]].<ref name="2018 Files" />

==Equipment==
At the [[time]] of his death, Branon flew a T-65 X-wing. He wore an orange [[flight suit]] and a white [[flak vest]]. He also donned a [[K-22995 light flight helmet]] colored red and white with black streaks above each brow.<ref name="Episode IV" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Naming and appearance===
John D. Branon was portrayed by [[Jack Klaff]] in the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], credited as "Red Four (John 'D')."<ref name="Episode IV" /> His surname "Branon" was identified in the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] by the [[2015]] digital trading card application, [[Star Wars: Card Trader|''Star Wars'': Card Trader]].<ref name="SWCT" /> In the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, the surname originated from [[Michael Knight]]'s [[2006]] strategy guide ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Prima Official Game Guide]]'',<ref name="EAW Guide">[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars: Empire at War'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> and Branon also appeared, voice only, prior to ''A New Hope'' in the [[1976]] [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of the film, written by [[Alan Dean Foster]].<ref name="novel">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref> The character was presumed to be named after special effects supervisor [[John Dykstra]].<ref name="Insider 95 Pirates">{{InsiderCite|95|Pirates of the Boards|Pirates of the Boards, Part 4}}</ref> A card in the [[2018 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files|2018 Topps ''Star Wars'' Galactic Files]] set erroneously assigns the [[Red Ten]] callsign to Branon.<ref name="2018 Files" />

===Storyboards, filming, and portrayal===
{{Quote|Do you mind if we blow you up?|Jack Klaff, repeating what George Lucas had asked him when he approached the actor for the role of Branon|<ref name="YouTube-1">{{YouTube|video=HdY7uTqDZhs|text=Jack Klaff Standing by. The Red 4 Interview - RS Prop Masters S03E10|channel=@RSPropMastersTV|name=RS Prop Masters}}</ref>}}
[[File:Johnd.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Some fans believed that Klaff portrayed the character that eventually became Col Takbright (pictured).]]
According to Klaff, he did not audition for the role of Branon and only received it when a fan of his who also served as a casting director for ''A New Hope'' cast a group of people, including Klaff, to play the pilots in the film.<ref name="RedDwarf">{{WebCite|url=https://reddwarf.co.uk/features/interviews/jack-klaff|text=Mr Flibble Talks To… Jack Klaff|author=Ellard, Andrew|date=2004-01-16|work=[https://reddwarf.co.uk Red Dwarf - The Official Website]|quote=I didn't even audition for it. I had a fan who was a casting director, who was casting ''Star Wars'' who knew me and got a group of people together as pilots.|archivedate=20200224072127}}</ref> When cast for the role of Branon, ''Star Wars'' creator [[George Lucas]] approached Klaff and asked him if he would mind if they blew him up.<ref name="YouTube-1" /> He agreed to play the character, and Branon's death scene was filmed in a matter of minutes<ref name="YouTube-2">{{YouTube|video=Jt3zQAy5hvw|text=X-Wing pilot Red 4 by JACK KLAFF - Star Wars 100 Interviews|channel=@StarWars100Interviews|name=Star Wars 100 Interviews}}</ref> at Stage 8 of [[Elstree Studios]], [[Wikipedia:London|London]] within the "Interior cockpit with blue backing" set at some point between [[June 28]] and [[June 29|29]], 1976.<ref name="Insider 95 Pirates" />

Originally, Klaff, whose character's designation was [[Blue Six]] in the script, was going to film his scenes with front projection, but Lucas decided to switch to a blue screen, and the character's callsign was changed to Red Four in post-production.<ref name="Insider 95 Pirates" /> During filming, the actor was placed in a cockpit set that rocked around in front of the blue screen, emulating the movement of the X-wing. After filming the scene, a wet cloth was placed over his face to clean the fumes that resulted from the X-wing's explosion.<ref name="YouTube-2" /> The character also had additional dialogue where he reported his callsign prior to the battle and exclaimed that he had downed a TIE fighter before being shot down,<ref name="Insider 95 Facts">{{InsiderCite|95|May The Facts Be With You: Part Two|May The Facts Be With You: Part Two: #51-100}}</ref> but they were not included in the film.<ref name="Episode IV" />

The annotations of special effects photographer [[Richard Edlund]] on artist [[Joe Johnston]]'s storyboards for the film revealed that a pilot named "Chewie" in the [[The Star Wars: From The Adventures of Luke Starkiller|third draft]] had its role divided into both Branon and Wedge Antilles due to the fact that the character of Chewbacca was also called by that name. In the storyboards, Branon is mentioned to have a scar across one eye and to have adjusted his targeting device during the battle,<ref name="Insider 95 Pirates" /> both of which are not shown in the film itself.<ref name="Episode IV" /> Another storyboard titled "Dog Fight" shows Branon with a helmet covering his entire face.<ref name="Lippincott Boards">{{Facebook|username=charles.lippincott.9|url=charles.lippincott.9/posts/pfbid02V7Bmcqdg2cfqdzsHSNbmpFxGCSJ3aP7GVMALYzVXBikDYE9hPcwk4FSAfRoTbeBYl|name=[[Charles Lippincott]]|date=2016-05-14|archiveurl=https://archive.is/L0s3h}}</ref>

===Actor misconception===
Some fans believed that Klaff portrayed Wedge Antilles in the briefing room scene, and the character in the scene was later nicknamed "Fake Wedge." While Antilles was played by [[Denis Lawson]] in the Battle of Yavin scenes, [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Pablo Hidalgo]] revealed that the character in the briefing room was not actually portrayed by Klaff, but by actor [[Colin Higgins]].<ref name="Mystery">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-mysteries-hunting-for-the-fake-wedge|series=Star Wars Mysteries|text=Hunting for the Fake Wedge}}</ref> The [[2017]] short story "[[Duty Roster]]," written by [[Jason Fry]] and published in the anthology ''[[From a Certain Point of View]]'', later [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] Higgins' role as Antilles into a separate character, Col Takbright.<ref name="DutyRoster" />
